narration: One of these clues is a set of bright streaks nobody can fully explain yet. Let's start there.
visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Mercury colorful crater); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.

candidates.title: MESSENGER Near Hokusai Crater Artist Concept
candidates.description: An artist rendering of the MESSENGER spacecraft is shown passing near the crater Hokusai and its extensive system of rays. Both the monochrome and enhanced color views of Mercury were obtained during MESSENGER second Mercury flyby.

candidates.title: Hemingway Color
candidates.description: Hemingway crater is seen in this color view of Mercury surface as seen by NASA MESSENGER spacecraft. Hemingway is the 130-km 81-mile diameter crater with a relatively brown floor and small patch of dark blue in its center.

candidates.title: Fading Away
candidates.description: This NAC image from MESSENGER’s second Mercury flyby shows a crater with a set of light-colored rays radiating outward from it. Such rays are formed when an impact excavates material from below the surface and throws it outward from the crater.

candidates.title: The Color Out of Space
candidates.description: Today's image features a color view of the southern pole of Mercury. About midway down the image, the edge of the large Chao Meng-Fu crater, which lies almost directly on the south pole, can be seen poking out from the shadows. Surrounding Chao Meng-Fu are Roerich, Lovecraft, Hurley and L'Engle crat
